own_solution.law: Q = mcΔT and Q = Pt, hence t = mcΔT/P = (2)(4186)(40)/1500 = 223.2533 s.
assumptions: The stated power is constant net power delivered to the water.
The water remains liquid throughout the temperature rise.
The specific heat capacity is constant at the stated value.
Heating the container requires negligible additional energy.

T47A8.regime: Single-phase liquid heating with constant specific heat; at ordinary atmospheric pressure, heating from 293 K to 333 K stays within this regime.

T17E2.regime: Single-phase liquid heating with constant specific heat; at ordinary atmospheric pressure, heating from 293 K to 333 K stays within this regime.

notes: The base problem uses the standard sensible-heating idealization. Adding water at the same starting temperature increases the heated mass to 3 kg without changing its initial temperature, giving t = (3)(4186)(40)/1500 = 334.88 s. The separate jugs have no physical connection to the heating process. Initial temperature is classified K because it can affect whether phase change occurs, although it does not affect the answer within the stated sensible-heating regime. Both temperature variants specify 293 K, and all jug variants specify 1 kg at the same starting temperature; their wording and attachment changes preserve those quantities.
